guide.title: Advanced Airways
guide.lead: When basic measures aren't enough, a trained provider places a supraglottic airway or an endotracheal tube. Everyone has a job: prepare, pre-oxygenate, confirm with waveform capnography, and keep watching it.

steps.title: Waveform capnography
steps.text: Recommended to confirm and continuously monitor placement. Normal EtCO₂ 35–45 mmHg.

steps.title: Listen
steps.text: Breath sounds on both sides; nothing over the epigastrium.

steps.title: Look
steps.text: Equal chest rise; secure the device; recheck after every move.

steps.title: In cardiac arrest
steps.text: 1 breath every 6 seconds (10 breaths/min) with continuous compressions.

groups.title: D – Displacement
items: Sudden loss of the capnography waveform: displaced until proven otherwise

groups.title: P – Pneumothorax
items: Absent breath sounds one side, rising resistance, falling SpO₂

items.label: ACLS Megacode
items.sub: Run an arrest with an advanced airway

quiz.q: Most reliable way to confirm and monitor an advanced airway:

quiz.explanation: A sudden drop to zero suggests displacement.

quiz.q: Ventilation rate after an advanced airway in cardiac arrest:
options: 1 breath every 6 seconds with continuous compressions

quiz.q: Before any intubation attempt, the assisting provider should first:
Breath sounds heard over the epigastrium after intubation suggest:
Why are supraglottic airways popular in cardiac arrest?
options: Quick insertion with fewer CPR interruptions

quiz.q: Capnography waveform suddenly disappears after moving the patient:
options: Suspect displacement and reassess at once

quiz.q: Which is an endotracheal tube feature?

flashcards.question: Gold standard to confirm and monitor placement
Supraglottic vs ETT
flashcards.answer: Supraglottic: above the cords, blind. ETT: through the cords, definitive.

flashcards.question: Other confirmation
flashcards.answer: Bilateral breath sounds, no epigastric sounds, equal chest rise.

flashcards.question: Sudden loss of waveform
flashcards.answer: Displacement (or loss of circulation): reassess immediately.

flashcards.question: Ventilation with an advanced airway in arrest

critical.scenario: After moving an intubated patient onto the stretcher, the capnography waveform disappears.
critical.question: Most likely meaning?

options.t: Tube displacement: reassess placement and breath sounds now

critical.kpi: Recognizes loss of capnography waveform as airway displacement

critical.scenario: An intubated patient becomes hard to ventilate: SpO₂ falling, no breath sounds on the right, trachea deviated left.
critical.question: Which DOPE cause?

options.f: Unilateral signs and tracheal shift point to pneumothorax.

critical.explanation: Needs decompression by a qualified provider.
critical.kpi: Differentiates DOPE causes of post-intubation deterioration

critical.scenario: A paramedic asks you to assist with intubation. SpO₂ is 88%.
critical.question: Your first action?

options.t: Pre-oxygenate with BVM or NRB to raise SpO₂ before the attempt
Remove the oxygen so they can see
Nothing until the tube is in

critical.kpi: Pre-oxygenates before an advanced airway attempt
